questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a good waiter and earn big tips
How to open a successful restaurant in New York
Why tipping is complicated and differs by place
The biggest tips ever given by famous customers
questions.why: Catherine calls tipping 'a really complicated issue', and they discuss how it differs by city.

questions.q: How does Sam feel about tipping?
options: She finds it very confusing
She always tips 20%
She never tips anyone
She thinks it should be banned
questions.why: She calls it 'a nightmare' and never knows who, how or how much to tip.

questions.q: In how many cities does William Beckett currently have restaurants?
options: One
Three
Four
Two
questions.why: Sam says two, London and Manchester; the New York one isn't open yet.

questions.q: What is the norm in London, according to William Beckett?
options: Nobody tips at all in restaurants
A service charge is usually on the bill
People always leave a tip in cash
Customers usually tip about 20%
questions.why: He says in London 'it's there, it's on your bill'.

questions.q: Why do some people prefer an automatic service charge?
options: It is always cheaper than leaving a tip
Waiters get more money at the end of the week
They don't have to think about or work out a tip
It is required by law in most British restaurants
questions.why: Catherine says they don't have to think about or try to calculate a tip.

questions.q: What does William Beckett say about tipping in New York?
options: Tipping is always included in the bill at the end
People only tip in expensive restaurants in Manhattan
Nobody expects a tip, as waiters get a good wage
Nobody says you must tip, but everyone feels they should
questions.why: He says there's 'a tacit pressure to tip'.

questions.q: What does William Beckett mean by saying you could 'theoretically' walk out without tipping?
options: It is possible, but people almost never do it
It is illegal and you could be fined for it
Most people do it and nobody really minds
Only tourists do it, because they don't know
questions.why: Catherine explains it's possible but very unlikely because of the tacit pressure.

questions.q: What do people like about not having a service charge, according to William Beckett?
options: Their final bill is always smaller at the end
They're free not to tip, even if they don't use it
The food is better because the chefs try harder
The waiters are friendlier and serve them faster
questions.why: Sam says people like that freedom not to tip, even if they don't actually use it.
